item.title: From Germany, with love: a letter to the UK | Klaus Brinkbäumer
item.description:
As Andy Burnham pushes to reopen Brexit, Berlin won’t say it, but the truth is, we just want you back

Dear British friends,

Germans are not the love-letter writing kind of people. When we write a letter, a complaint is usually not far off. But we cannot complain about you. About other things, yes: transatlantic relations, or Trump, ja, ja. Or our own chancellor, who every morning talks about reforms which, by the evening, we know will never get done. But when I think about Britain I feel only one thing: longing.

Klaus Brinkbäumer, a former executive editor at Der Spiegel, is an author and podcast and TV host in Germany

item.title: Ukraine war briefing: Trump ‘open’ to Kyiv getting Nato-like mutual defence guarantee, says Kushner
item.description:
US presidential envoy also says he believes Moscow is ‘comfortable’ with a guarantee while France calls for fresh look at Ukraine joining Nato. What we know on day 1,731

US envoy Jared Kushner has said Donald Trump is open to extending Ukraine a security guarantee similar to Nato’s mutual defence clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. French president Emmanuel Macron meanwhile urged Kyiv’s allies to “reopen the question” of Ukraine becoming a member of the military alliance. Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, told a press conference in Germany: “From America’s perspective, giving an Article 5-like security guarantee is a really, really big deal. And I think that that’s something that President Trump is open to, but obviously it has to be in America’s interest to do that. We also have to make sure that it’s part of a broader security package.”

Kushner’s comments came after Ukraine’s allies gathered for a summit of the “coalition of the willing” in Berlin with Volodymyr Zelenskyy to emphasise support for Kyiv nearly five years since Russia’s 2022 invasion, and to push for a European role in future peace negotiations. Kushner added on Thursday that “we’ve gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept, where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5 ”. He noted that went with Moscow’s intention to “not have another war” when this conflict was over, while acknowledging “skepticism” over the position.

Macron called on Ukraine’s allies to do the “maximum” to deliver the air defence systems it needed, as well as looking again at Ukraine joining Nato. “Faced with the maximalist nature of the Russian position, I believe we need to reopen the question of Ukraine’s accession to Nato,” the French president said in Berlin. “Everyone who has the capacity to provide the means to defend and protect Ukrainian citizens must do so now,” he said, adding the priority was to deploy anti-missile systems and interceptors.

The coalition’s summit was co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, Britain and France shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between Trump, Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. China, Russia and the US said after their talks they had agreed to a peace statement, but the declaration made no mention of the war in Ukraine. The European coalition’s meeting in Berlin expressed indignation at the trilateral’s cosy optics, reports Rebecca Bailey. “Mr Putin is not our friend and ⁠will never be,” the Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, said in a rejoinder to Trump.

German chancellor Friedrich Merz said he expected new Ukraine peace talks would “take place soon”, with Europe now set to have a seat at the table alongside the US, Russia and Ukraine. Merz, speaking in Berlin, did not give a date and added that “we are looking for locations on neutral ground”, naming the United Arab Emirates as a possible location. British prime minister Andy Burnham said: “I hope that message is heard very clearly in Moscow. For as long as it takes, we will be there at the side of Ukraine and we will not falter.”

Putin said Russia’s response to the bombing of the Kerch Bridge to Crimea would be “painful”, after Ukraine attacked the strategic connection for the third time this week. The Russian president claimed he had considered agreeing to local ceasefires until the Kerch road bridge was destroyed, reports Dan Sabbagh and Jakub Krupa. “After the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, we will not negotiate,” Putin said.

A ⁠fire broke out in a three-story building in ⁠the Obolonskyi ⁠district ​in northern Kyiv after it was hit ⁠by missile debris, the city’s mayor said on Friday. Emergency ‌services were heading to the ‌scene, Vitali Klitschko added on Telegram. A series of explosions were reportedly heard in the city in the early hours.

A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged the historic Saint Volodymyr Cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. “Russia has been terrorising Kyiv with drones all day ... At least four people are known to be injured so far, and one person was killed,” prime minister Sergiy Koretsky said. The Dutch embassy building sustained minor damage, Dutch foreign minister Tom Berendsen said. Ukraine’s top diplomat, Andriy Sybiga, said debris had fallen on the grounds of the foreign ministry and the Brazilian embassy as well.

item.title: UK-EU reset talks will go ‘down to the wire’ as crunch summit approaches
item.description:
Britain makes concessions on youth mobility scheme as negotiations on food and farming go down to the wire

British and European negotiators were closing in on a reset deal on Thursday night as they provisionally agreed to allow 100,000 EU citizens to come to the UK every year under a new mobility scheme.

It is understood the EU dropped its demands at the last minute that EU students would pay home tuition fees if they attended British universities in a last minute concession to get the deal over the line.

The UK and the EU plan to establish formal talks for the first time about sending rejected asylum seekers to third-country hubs, according to a leaked document.

A draft of a joint statement expected to be signed by Andy Burnham and Ursula von der Leyen at a summit on Friday morning states that both sides will establish “a structured dialogue” to discuss “returns to third countries”.
